note: Generated by design/tools/boss_choir.py. World units. A Voice's shapes are local, +x toward the ring's centre; polylines are lists of points. The hood is closed by the mouth's two lips.

core.note: gold while singing: the weak point

halo.note: an arc behind the hood, pearl; brightens with the Voice's own note

wavefronts.note: three arcs leaving the open mouth, one beat to fade

numbers.singing: a Voice's mouth is open from the step it fires until one beat later; shots ring off a closed hood

ring.turn: one revolution every 16 bars; the direction reverses whenever a Voice dies
ring.centre: the players' centroid when it arrives; it follows the centroid at 60 wu/s, kept 700 wu from every wall
ring.order: Voice k stands at k x 45 degrees and owns note k of the scale, so the ring is the scale and opposite Voices are a fifth apart

camera.note: eased over the entrance bar, so the whole Round is in the frame from inside it; back to 1 over a bar at the end

contact.note: a hood hurts by touch only while its mouth is open (from the step it fires until one beat later: the same window in which it can be hurt). A silent hood is drawn at 0.6 of its level and a ship flies through it unharmed. The strings never hurt, except while the cage burns. Ruled 2026-11-13: with every hood hurting, a ship that crosses the Round lost a cell eleven times a fight and the bot that does not dodge lost half its runs here; the Choir's danger is its song, not its furniture

phases.name: Unison

call.pattern: a fan at the nearest player, 11 degrees apart

phases.caller: moves one Voice clockwise every bar
phases.note: fire comes from in front, then from behind: turn with the song

phases.name: Canon

call.pattern: a fan at the nearest player, 11 degrees apart

response.who: every other live Voice, clockwise from the caller
response.when: one eighth after the Voice before it
response.pattern: a fan at the nearest player, 14 degrees apart

phases.caller: moves one live Voice clockwise every bar
phases.note: the answer runs round the ring like a wave: move with it, not against it

phases.name: Fugue

call.who: two callers, as far apart as the live Voices allow
call.pattern: a stream that sweeps 80 degrees across the nearest player over the bar; the second caller sweeps the other way

phases.caller: callers and answerers swap every bar
phases.note: the Round has shrunk; two sweeps cross once a bar and the crossing is the gap

phases.name: Solo

orbit.note: the ring is gone: the last Voices circle the nearest player

call.pattern: a ring; alternate rings turned half a step

heldNote.note: a dashed line for one bar, then a beam from the open mouth that sweeps on beats 1 and 2 of the next

phases.note: one voice left: it is hurt at 1.5x while it sings

cage.rule: the strings between neighbouring live Voices show danger dashes for one bar, then burn as beams for two beats from the next downbeat. A string needs both its Voices: every dead Voice opens two gaps in the cage

numbers.deadVoice: its beat becomes a rest: nothing fires, nothing sounds. A dead caller is skipped; a dead answerer leaves the call unanswered

neighbour.note: the octagon: a thin line between neighbouring live Voices, coloured from one Voice's hue to the other's

call.note: between a singing Voice and the Voice that will answer it: a standing wave drawn as its two envelopes, the singer's hue at one end, white in the middle, the answerer's hue at the other. Light only: it never hurts

music.patch: the pad patch as a voice: attack 20 ms, release one beat, reverb send 0.5; one note per sung step
music.rule: a Voice sings its own note whenever it fires, so the fight plays the scale: in Unison each bar is root, fifth, root, fifth, one degree higher every bar; in Canon the answer runs up the scale in eighths; every death takes a note out of the tune for good
music.death: the dying Voice's note falls a fourth over one beat into the reverb
music.cage: the telegraph tick on every beat of the telegraph bar, the impact sample on the burn
music.heldNote: the last Voice's note held for the whole telegraph bar, rising an octave as the beam fires

hues.rule: eight hues 45 degrees apart round the OKLCH wheel (lightness 0.80, chroma 96% of the gamut), starting at the Track's first enemy hue; any hue within 25 degrees of the danger colour moves to the nearer edge of that band. This is the one boss that wears every colour

pearl.use: halos, faces and strings at rest

hues.singing: a singing Voice is drawn white-hot over its own hue with a two-arm flare across its mouth and a gold core: the gold is the weak point

numbers.entrance: on the Drop's downbeat the Voices warp in clockwise, one every eighth, each singing its note as it lands: a rising scale. On bar 2 all eight sing together and the name card THE CHOIR holds for two bars; firing starts on bar 3
numbers.voiceDeath: the hood splits along its axis and falls outward; its two neighbour strings snap back to the neighbours with a white flash; the ring stops for one beat and turns the other way
numbers.death: the eight hoods return as outlines in their own hues for one bar and sing the last chord (D, A, D), every string white; then they shatter outward clockwise, one every eighth, each a large kill, the last as a boss break: three rings, 300+ sparks, the 30 px distortion ring, 50 ms hit-stop, then 220 Shards
numbers.coop: health x (1 + 0.5 x (players - 1)); fans aim at the nearest player to the singing Voice; in Solo each Voice circles a different player while two live
